clue.text: He goes to work on foot

definitions.text: He goes to work on foot

parts.words: He goes to work on foot
parts.note: reads like a commuter who walks to the office, but means someone whose work is done on people's feet

explanation.surface: A man who walks to his job every morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to work on' means 'sets about treating', not 'travels to his job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiropodist-style practitioner tends toenails and soles, so feet are the place where this worker does the job.

clue.text: Lamps made from living matter

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the clue word, which are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Lights constructed out of organic material.
explanation.definitionFit: Protoplasm, the living substance of cells, is often shortened to this word.

clue.text: Their staying powers are apparently exhausted

definitions.text: Their staying powers are apparently exhausted

parts.words: Their staying powers are apparently exhausted
parts.note: 'staying powers' sounds like stamina, but means their power to stay in a country has run out

explanation.surface: People who have run out of stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: Staying power usually means endurance; here it is the right to stay in the country, which has been taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: People expelled from a country by the state have lost the right of residence there.

clue.text: Are round-the-table discussions so long-winded?

parts.note: the Latin pieces of the answer mean 'around' and 'speaking', echoing 'round-the-table discussions', and the word means long-winded

explanation.surface: A grumble that conferences always drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into Latin circum (around) and locutory (to do with speaking): a round-table discussion, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Talk that goes round the point in many words is wordy and indirect.

clue.text: Revives jamborees ?

definitions.meaning: recovers strength, as a patient or a falling market does
large gatherings, such as mass meetings of scouts or political supporters

explanation.definitionFit: A patient who recovers strength does this, and big mass meetings or marches are also called by the same word.

clue.text: Dexterity in making leg-hits

indicators.note: the letters of the hyphenated word are used to make a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A batsman's skill shown in scoring with shots to the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg-hit is a cricket shot to the leg side; the surface keeps the solver thinking of a batsman's skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is manual skill, so the word means deftness.

clue.text: This course includes greens

parts.note: reads as a meal course with vegetables, but the course is a sporting one with putting greens

explanation.surface: A dinner course served with vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' and 'greens' both suggest a meal; the course is a golf course and the greens are where players putt.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport is played over a course of holes, each ending on a closely mown putting surface.

clue.text: They are meant to be taken seriously

definitions.text: They are meant to be taken seriously

parts.words: They are meant to be taken seriously
parts.note: sounds like remarks that are not jokes, but plays on the idiom of taking a solemn vow

explanation.surface: Statements nobody should laugh at.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'takes' a vow, as in a court or ceremony, which is the sense of 'taken' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sworn promises are solemn declarations, made before a witness or a god.

clue.text: Those free to 'ay cricket

parts.note: points to the Free ..., a long-established English amateur cricket club, the dropped H mimicking a rustic accent

explanation.surface: Countryfolk at liberty to play a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Free Foresters are an English amateur cricket club founded in the 1850s; forest workers are also the people of the woods, which the dropped-H 'ay hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who work in woodland are known by this name, and an amateur cricket club uses it with 'Free' in front.

clue.text: Cause of low spirits for many in war-time

definitions.text: Cause of low spirits for many in war-time

parts.words: Cause of low spirits for many in war-time
parts.note: 'spirits' looks like morale, but means motor spirit, the fuel that was rationed during the war

explanation.surface: What made people gloomy during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' is an old British word for motor fuel, so 'low spirits' are low tanks, not low morale.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime rationing meant drivers had too little motor fuel to go around.

clue.text: It oft proclaims the man, said Polonius

definitions.text: It oft proclaims the man, said Polonius

parts.words: It oft proclaims the man, said Polonius
parts.note: quotes Polonius's advice to Laertes in Hamlet, 'for the ... oft proclaims the man', about dressing well

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare quoted with its speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Polonius tells his son to buy fine but not gaudy clothes, since what a man wears tells others what he is.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted word means clothing, which Polonius says reveals a man's character.

clue.text: This seat may put one out

definitions.text: This seat may put one out

parts.words: This seat may put one out
parts.note: sounds like an inconvenient chair, but refers to an aircraft seat that fires the pilot clear

explanation.surface: An uncomfortable chair that inconveniences whoever sits there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one out' looks like 'annoy someone'; it means literally throw the occupant out of the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: In a military jet, the pilot's seat can be blasted clear of the cockpit in an emergency.

clue.text: Complaint sorted out with double rum and gin

indicators.note: the drinks' letters are sorted into a new order, so they are rearranged
a double measure, read as the word written twice

explanation.surface: A grievance settled with a double rum and a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' gives RUM twice; 'sorted out' rearranges RUMRUM with GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A low grumbling expression of discontent is a mutter of protest.

clue.text: The dangers of policy-makers

parts.note: sounds like political perils, but the policies are insurance policies, which underwriters write against hazards

explanation.surface: The perils facing politicians who make policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policy-makers' are insurers writing policies, and what they cover are the hazards insured against.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers speak of the hazards they underwrite, and the word also means simply dangers.

clue.text: Time to read letters

definitions.meaning: a period, as in a short stint of work
to name the letters of a word in order

explanation.surface: A period set aside for reading the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint or period is one sense; naming a word's letters in order is the other.

clue.text: Not a mound raised to commemorate a battle

definitions.text: Not a mound raised to commemorate a battle

parts.words: Not a mound raised to commemorate a battle
parts.note: plays on scrap meaning a fight, so a heap of scrap sounds like a battle memorial, which it is not

explanation.surface: A pile that is no war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap is slang for a fight, so the answer read literally sounds like a battle mound; it is a dump of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded metal and rubbish is where useless things are thrown.

clue.text: A famous bowman in the plot is a revolutionary

indicators.note: the bowman and the A are placed inside the plot of land

parts.note: a plot of land is a site
William Tell, the Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.surface: A legendary archer is caught up in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The plot' looks like a conspiracy but is a building site; 'revolutionary' means something that revolves, as a moon orbits a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon or spacecraft circles a planet, so it is something that orbits.

clue.text: After opening bars, Green has to turn in

indicators.note: shows the colour comes after the opening bars in the answer

parts.note: the opening bars of a piece of music are its intro
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: After the first notes of the song, a singer called Green has to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert is green in heraldry; the answer is used here as a verb, to turn inwards.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to direct inward, as a mind turns its thoughts upon itself.

clue.text: Their occupants are intent on leisure ?

definitions.text: Their occupants are intent on leisure ?

parts.words: Their occupants are intent on leisure
parts.note: 'intent' splits as 'in tent', so the occupants are relaxing under canvas

explanation.surface: People determined to take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'intent' as 'in tent': holidaymakers at camps for resting.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday sites with tents or huts are places where people stay to relax.

clue.text: Othello worried about one learning to dance

annotationWithheld.why: Othello worried about one learning to dance (7): MORISCO; MOOR (Othello) with I (one) gives only six letters of the seven, and no reading of 'learning' supplies the S and C soundly
annotationWithheld.clue: Othello worried about one learning to dance

clue.text: We are put up to occupy these seats

definitions.text: We are put up to occupy these seats

parts.words: We are put up to occupy these seats
parts.note: seats that are put up on horses and occupied by riders, not seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: Seats installed for people to sit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' means placed on a horse's back, and riders occupy them.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders sit on leather seats strapped to a horse's back.

clue.text: One loathes to have them

parts.note: one who loathes has strong dislikes, the plural noun of loathing

explanation.surface: Things a person is reluctant to own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loathes to have' looks like 'is loath to have'; the word is a plural noun meaning things one loathes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong aversions are the plural noun for dislikes, and loathing someone means having them.

clue.text: Bird gets it after seed

indicators.note: puts the second word after the seed in the answer

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A bird finds something after pecking at seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird of fields and meadows, such as the meadow kind.

clue.text: He takes steps to keep you in the running

definitions.text: He takes steps to keep you in the running

parts.words: He takes steps to keep you in the running
parts.note: sounds like someone helping a candidate, but means a runner setting the speed in a race

explanation.surface: A supporter acting to keep a candidate in contention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes steps' and 'in the running' sound figurative; they are literal for a runner who sets the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race this runner sets the speed for another competitor.

clue.text: This Dickensian was a rogue

parts.note: Rogue is the first name of the waterman villain in Our Mutual Friend

explanation.surface: A Dickens character who was a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Our Mutual Friend, the villain is literally named Rogue, so 'was a rogue' is both his character and his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gave his Thames waterman villain this surname, with Rogue as his first name.

clue.text: Records to talk about with us out of the way

indicators.note: the letters of 'us' are put aside from the longer word

parts.note: to talk about something is to discuss it

explanation.surface: Archives that one must talk over once we are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the way' removes the U and the second S from DISCUSS, leaving DISCS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gramophone records are flat round discs of vinyl or shellac.

clue.text: Costers might make good bodyguards

indicators.note: the street traders' word might make another word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Barrow-boys would be useful as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Costers, short for costermongers, are London street traders selling fruit from barrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed guards accompanying someone are protective companions.

clue.text: The Baker Street unemployed ?

parts.note: Baker Street is Sherlock Holmes's address, but here a baker makes loaves, and idle people loaf

explanation.surface: Jobless people on Sherlock Holmes's street.
explanation.walkthrough: Baker Street is a London street, Holmes's address; a baker's street would be full of loaves, and idlers who loaf about are named for doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle people who hang about doing nothing are known as layabouts.

clue.text: Apparently not all a player needs

definitions.text: Apparently not all a player needs

parts.words: Apparently not all a player needs
parts.note: an actor needs a role, and the word for a role also means a fraction rather than the whole

explanation.surface: A player always needs more than this.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor needs a role, and the word for a role also means a portion, so it seems to be less than all.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's role is also the word for a portion of a whole.

clue.text: Synopsis needs crafty cuts, without taking chances

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled word goes round the other piece
crafty suggests artful reworking, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: doing something on spec is doing it speculatively, taking a chance

explanation.surface: A summary needs clever editing, with no gambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is outside: CTUS (an anagram of CUTS, from 'crafty') goes round ON SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A general survey or summary gives an overview of a subject.
